description:
I’m a student in IT security and digital trust, passionate about building secure and reliable systems. For this challenge, I want to create astronaut health monitoring software that protects sensitive data through encryption, access control, and data integrity.

I’m looking for teammates with skills in:

Front-end or mobile development (dashboards and alerts)

Data analysis or AI/ML (health data trends)

UI/UX design

Backend or database experience
summary: We developed SENTRA – Mission Control, an integrated astronaut health-monitoring and decision-support prototype built with React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Nginx, and Docker. The platform centralizes physiological indicators, tracks historical trends, flags abnormal readings with contextual recommendations, promotes daily preventive habits via safe gamification, and performs hybrid AI health assessments including a Random Forest stress-detection model calibrated to each astronaut’s personal baseline.
details: SENTRA – Mission Control is an astronaut health-monitoring and decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to bridge the gap between raw physiological tracking and actionable onboard medical interpretation during space missions. Built on a containerized client-server architecture using React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL 16, Nginx, and Docker, the platform centralizes biometric data, tracks historical trends, flags abnormal statuses, and encourages daily preventive habits through medically safe gamification. What makes SENTRA creative is its hybrid analytical engine—combining explainable rule-based logic with a Random Forest machine learning model trained on the WESAD physiological dataset and calibrated to each astronaut's personal resting baseline via Z-score normalization (achieving 95.6% accuracy and a 94.6% F1-score in 5-fold participant-grouped cross-validation). Throughout development, the team prioritized scientific rigor, data privacy—using PostgreSQL Row-Level Security, role separation, and JWT authentication—and honest uncertainty handling by explicitly distinguishing not_assessed health categories from normal results so that unmeasured metrics are never presented as clinical diagnoses.
